evidence: STRUCTURE (static; supports a graded spread): tests/scoring.toml has gates render=0.0 and constraints=0.0, weights functional 0.6 / polish 0.2 / visual 0.2, floors functional=0.05. score.py and test.sh are byte-identical to the frozen template (diff clean), so reward = weighted mean when both gates pass and functional > 0.05. Only the two gates are all-or-nothing, each a single binary prerequisite (render: wrong password refused, then valid sign-in renders a workspace; constraints: job and candidate created through the UI and seen from an independent Observer context). These are deliberate prerequisites, not the scored signal. Scored suite: functional has 43 binary criteria weighted 0.5-2.5 (total 58.5; the largest single criterion is 2.5, 4.3% of functional), aggregation weighted_mean. Polish has 5 binary criteria (3, 3, 2, 1.5, 2.5; total 12). Visual has 5 likert points=5 criteria with described anchors at every level, weight 1.2 each. The functional prompt says 'score EACH criterion independently, continue after failures and keep successful observations. A failed sibling verdict is not evidence against another row' (functional/prompt.md:13) and adds re-setup on a new job when a setup step fails; polish/prompt.md:12 and visual/prompt.md:12 also say to judge each criterion independently. Apart from the gate-duplicate browser check, no single precondition controls all criteria. Live-update dependence covers functional live_board/msg_exchange/unread_counts/unread_scrolled_up/seen (9.5/58.5) and polish live_board/live_thread (6/12). Bulk/undo dependence covers about 10/58.5. Conversations and roles are separate clusters. SIMULATION (my own in-memory arithmetic over the actual judge.toml weights and the score.py formula, assuming the listed rows pass and all others fail; per-criterion independence assumed; files evidence/40/sim40.py.txt and evidence/40/sim40_output.txt, sha256 9dfe04d0... and 0308ef00...): golden-like 1.0; no live updates 0.7526; no bulk/no undo 0.8321; no live + no bulk/undo + no stale check 0.4615; board only, no conversations 0.55; CRUD+roles only, ugly 0.1372; gate-pass minimal (job and candidate only) 0.0 through the functional floor. The rubric's shape therefore yields a spread across partial apps rather than all-or-nothing. MEASUREMENT GAP (why this is not a Pass): raw-evidence-index.json scope states verbatim 'Full configured grading/workload, reward discrimination/ranking and Oracle/target scores are absent'. The indexed artifacts are scripted golden observations only. REVIEW_POLICY.md 'Runtime and model evidence' requires a hash-bound reward-discrimination record from mutated weak apps. None exists, and the skill forbids upgrading an unmeasured claim to Pass. RESIDUAL COLLAPSE RISKS (unmeasured): (1) At test.sh:224-227, if the scored rewardkit run fails or exceeds its 11100 s budget, test.sh exits with the gate-stage reward.json, whose scored dimensions are 0 (score.py sets the weights to 0.0 when scored_data is None). The whole reward then collapses to 0 regardless of app quality. The functional protocol has 13 sequential protocols (Z,S,M,L,C,B,N,T,U,K,R,V,A,D), about 10 accounts, many independent contexts, replays and 15 s waits, under a judge timeout of 9000. It runs longest for the best apps because broken features fail fast, so a near-golden app is the most exposed to this all-or-nothing outcome. Workload is unmeasured. (2) Long conjunctive rows concentrate correlated failures. For example, hro_activity requires a correct line for every successful action across S..V, and hro_undo_restores/hro_undo_once depend on the B protocol's three-card move, which cannot be set up again without bulk selection. This compresses partial-quality apps toward the same score bands. It reduces the spread but does not eliminate it. Counterexample attempts: a plausible broken app (static board, dead live channel) cannot score broadly, because the gate, the independent-context checks and the 15 s live rows zero those parts. A conforming alternative that sends moves over sockets keeps credit only where its requests can be replayed. hireops_rules.md:123 permits polling, SSE and sockets, and the prompt replays only observed requests, so this is a coverage issue for other rows, not a reward-shape defect here. I found no credible structural Fail for row 40; the measured discrimination record is missing.
suggested_fix: Produce the hash-bound reward-discrimination record the policy requires: run the full configured verifier (or at least the scored suite) on the golden plus 2-3 mutated weak apps (for example live updates disabled; bulk/undo removed; conversations removed). Record the per-dimension and final rewards and the functional judge wall time, confirming a spread and that the near-golden run finishes inside the 9000 s judge and 11100 s suite budgets.
